items.title: Derek Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995
items.q: Now she comes out and she’s got these wonderful parts, what a wonderful singer. And we’re playing and we’re playing and playing.

ctx.x: No, no, I didn’t know this was coming. I didn’t know this from a hole in the wall. But he comes out there and proceeds to do like ten minutes on me. And I’m sitting there. And it’s my first day on the job. And I’m steaming. But it all worked out. Everybody had a good laugh at that. The band was killing themselves with laughter. But we had like many

experiences. It was great as a pianist, I mean once a wonderful lady, an opera singer, Marilyn Horne came on. And you know, so we had a rehearsal, a very fading piece of music, a yellowing piece of music, and just like you described with the flycrap. And so I’m just playing it. And you know I’ll read anything. And I’m playing it, but you don’t have the feeling. You’ve got to be born to that kind of music like I’m born to play jazz. But I’m reading and I’m reading. And we’re going on. And so fine, we get to the…
That must have been, that must have been a blast. Tell me some of the other interesting people that you accompanied when you played on the show.
